item.description: AAEON uCOM-Q6490 is a SMARC 2.1-compliant System-on-Module (SoM) built around the Qualcomm Dragonwing QCS6490 octa-core SoC, designed for robotics, healthcare, industrial automation, and digital signage applications. The 82 × 50 mm module ships with up to 16GB LPDDR5 memory and 64GB UFS storage, and its standard MXM 3.0 edge connector exposes SDIO 3.0, PCIe 3.0, dual GbE, USB 3.1, and USB 2.0 interfaces, along with UARTs, SPI, I2C, I2S, GPIOs, and a DisplayPort 1.4 output supporting 2K at 60Hz. item.title: M5Stack Paper Mono – An ESP32-S3 e-paper development board with 3.97-inch touchscreen, LoRa, and NFC
item.description: M5Stack introduced the PaperColor ESP32-S3 devkit last May, but if you prefer faster refresh rates, the new Paper Mono should be a better option. The kit is based on a 3.97-inch monochrome e-Paper touch display and also supports LoRa and NFC long-range and short-range connectivity. The devkit features 8MB PSRAM, 16MB flash, a microSD card slot, a PDM microphone and buzzer for audio interaction, a 6-axis IMU, an RTC, and a few buttons and an RGB LED. The Paper Mono doesn’t come with any expansion port and is powered by a USB-C port and a 1150 mAh battery. A Lite version is also offered without LoRa and NFC. item.description: We recently noted that NXP expanded its MCX A series with the MCX A5 Cortex-M33 family, integrating 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet, topology discovery, and PQC for industrial connectivity. item.title: Why are people suddenly adding Apple Lightning cables to Raspberry Pi Pico 2 boards?
item.description: Yesterday I received an email with the subject “Rp2350 pi pico 2 modified one”. I found the request funny because it features an illustration with a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 board and an Apple Lightning cable, and I had no idea why somebody would do that at the time. Coming to my physical address (today!) was also humorous considering where I live… Nevertheless, I decided to share the screenshot above on X, and quickly found out the reasons: jailbreaking/bypassing iDevices with Apple A12/A13 CPUs using the usbliter8 boot ROM exploit by Paradigm Shift. One X user (stacksmashing) even replied: “I literally have this on my desk right now”. The original blog post on Paradigm Shift and the code on GitHub have been taken down due to a U.S. federal court order in a trade-secrets lawsuit filed by Magnet Forensics. item.title: Pine64 hits pause on Linux devices due to RAM and eMMC shortage/high prices
item.description: While some companies keep increasing prices, the Pine64 community has now announced they don’t intend to manufacture Linux devices due to the current RAM and eMMC flash shortage and related high prices. Pine64 started with the launch of the Pine A64 development board in 2015, and since then they have launched more Arm and RISC-V Linux SBCs, Linux smartphones, and Linux tablets and e-Readers. We used to get several announcements per year, but this year so far, we only covered one: the Pine64 PineVoice. But it’s not a Linux device, and instead, a smart speaker based on a BL602 RISC-V microcontroller. Here’s the full (unedited) announcement published on Telegram, which you should also find on other Pine64 channels: Hi everyone! Just a quick reminder that due to the current DRAM/eMMC shortage, there isn’t any plans to continue producing more Linux devices in the near future. item.title: Pi-Ener-lite – A compact 18650 UPS board for Raspberry Pi Zero with RTC and fuel gauge
item.description: Designed by ACE Design Studio in China, the Pi-Ener-lite is a dedicated UPS board made specifically for the Raspberry Pi Zero series. It features a standard flat-top 18650 lithium-ion battery holder and switches to battery power when external power is lost, while supporting simultaneous charging and discharging. The Pi-Ener-lite connects to the bottom of the Raspberry Pi Zero via seven spring-loaded pogo pins that handle both power delivery and I2C data communication, leaving the top GPIO header free for other HATs or expansions. Pi-Ener-lite specifications: Compatibility – Raspberry Pi Zero series SBCs USB – 1x USB Type-C port for charging Misc Power switch DS1307 real-time clock (RTC) chip with a CR1220 coin cell battery holder 7x spring pogo pins for power delivery and I2C data Power Management Battery Support – Standard flat-top 18650 lithium-ion cell; supports simultaneous charging and discharging Charging current – 1A @ 5V Output current – 2.5A [...] The post Pi-Ener-lite – A compact 18650 UPS board for Raspberry Pi Zero with RTC and fuel gauge appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.

item.title: EITWatch open-source ESP32-S3 smartwatch implements planar EIT hand gesture recognition
item.description: Researchers from Northwestern University have introduced EITWatch, an open-source ESP32-S3-based EIT (Electrical Impedance Tomography) gesture-sensing system that fits within a standard smartwatch footprint. It relies on a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 board and eight electrodes arranged on the back of the case to detect hand gestures via impedance changes caused by muscle and tendon movement beneath the skin. Unlike other wrist-EIT systems that use circumferential electrode bands, EITWatch places all eight electrodes on the back of the smartwatch case. The sensing area consists of a 31 mm electrode ring that fits within a standard 40 mm watch case, while a 20 mm PCB extension carries the discrete analog front end (AFE). EITWatch hardware specifications: Wireless board – XIAO ESP32-S3 SoC – Espressif ESP32-S3R8 CPU – Dual-core Tensilica LX7 microcontroller up to 240 MHz with vector instructions for AI acceleration Memory – 512KB SRAM, 8MB PSRAM Wireless – Wi-Fi 4 and [...] The post EITWatch open-source ESP32-S3 smartwatch implements planar EIT hand gesture recognition appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.

item.title: Giada DK320 digital signage player and Edge AI embedded PC supports up to the Intel Core 5 315 Wildcat Lake processor

item.title: Gemma Translator multilingual interpreter runs locally on Raspberry Pi 5 with the LiteRT runtime
item.description: Gemma Translator is an open-source project for the Raspberry Pi 5 that acts as a multilingual interpreter running locally without access to the cloud using Google Gemma 4 and LiteRT runtime. It’s a project built by three Google engineers with the help of Google Antigravity. It includes code to run an on-device, fully offline voice translator/interpreter using Gemma 4 E2B (2.3B effective / ~5.1B total parameters with per-layer embeddings) and the LiteRT runtime. item.title: PewCB One Desktop PCB fabrication system enables rapid prototyping at home
item.description: PewCB One is a desktop PCB prototyping system designed to accelerate hardware development by manufacturing PCBs at home or in the office in a few hours or less, instead of waiting days for a PCB to come back from the factory. item.title: Comu is a $6 tiny CH32V203 RISC-V development board that fits inside a USB port
item.description: Over the years, we have seen several tiny “omu” USB boards that share this “fits-in-a-USB-port” form factor. It started with the Tomu, based on a Silicon Labs EFM32 Cortex-M0+, followed by the Fomu with a Lattice iCE40 FPGA, Qomu with an EOS S3 Cortex-M4F MCU and FPGA, and the Somu, a tiny FIDO2 security key. Icy Electronics has now introduced Comu, another tiny development board based on the 144 MHz WCH CH32V203 RISC-V MCU. While measuring just 13 x 9.4 mm (slightly smaller than a microSD card), the board still packs two white LEDs, four capacitive touch buttons, and six GPIOs exposed through test pads. It is designed for bare-metal programming, custom USB HID projects, and USB packet experimentation. Comu specifications: MCU – WCH CH32V203V203F8 CPU – Single-core 32-bit RISC-V clocked at 144MHz Memory – 20KB SRAM Storage – 224KB Flash (64KB of 0-wait Flash and 160KB of normal Flash) [...] The post Comu is a $6 tiny CH32V203 RISC-V development board that fits inside a USB port appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.

item.title: MaTouch ESP32-S3 MaUWB board integrates 3.95-inch touchscreen and UWB module for indoor positioning and ranging
item.description: Makerfabs MaTouch ESP32-S3 MaUWB is a development board that combines an ESP32-S3 wireless MCU, a 3.95-inch touchscreen display, and a UWB module for indoor positioning and ranging applications. The board can be used as a portable positioning terminal. It uses a trilateration algorithm with up to three fixed UWB anchors to calculate the tag’s coordinates in real time. The MaUWB chipset operates on UWB Channel 5 (6489.6 MHz) and supports up to 8 anchors and 64 tags. For portable use, the board includes a LiPo battery connector, charging circuit, and battery level monitoring.
